message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Fresh sweep completed using the monitored product list in Products.txt. I found two credible, clearly product-matched vulnerability update groups reported on 11 June 2026 within the daily monitoring window: Google Chrome and Ubuntu/Ubuntu-packaged components. No credible fresh MongoDB, Cisco Nexus/UCS/Fabric Extender, SonicWall, FortiOS, Microsoft, Adobe, VMware, database, or other monitored-product advisories survived the 24-hour freshness and relevance checks for this run.

**Finding 1: Google Chrome desktop security update**

- Product: Google Chrome
- Issue: Multiple Chrome security fixes in Stable Channel 149.0.7827.114/.115, including CVE-2026-12007, CVE-2026-12008, CVE-2026-12009, and additional high-severity CVEs listed by Google
- Severity: Critical and High, as stated for highlighted Chrome CVEs
- Description: Google published a Stable Channel desktop update for Windows, macOS, and Linux with 28 security fixes. The highlighted issues include critical use-after-free and input-validation vulnerabilities, plus multiple high-severity browser component flaws.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes Google Chrome, and the advisory explicitly names Chrome desktop Stable Channel builds.
- Source: Google Chrome Releases: https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/

**Finding 2: Ubuntu security notices published 11 June 2026**

- Product: Ubuntu and Ubuntu-packaged components
- Issue: USN-8426-1, USN-8423-1, USN-8424-1, USN-8422-1, USN-8421-1, and USN-8420-1; includes CVE-2026-46333, CVE-2026-43284, CVE-2026-8836, CVE-2026-41283, CVE-2026-48681, CVE-2026-44917, CVE-2026-46447, CVE-2026-45491, and CVE-2026-45591 among others
- Severity: Not clearly stated in the Ubuntu notices
- Description: Canonical published several Ubuntu Security Notices covering Linux kernel Azure vulnerabilities, lwIP buffer-overflow issues, Ubuntu Kylin Software Center local privilege escalation, Mistral API policy enforcement flaws, Ironic file/path and boot-parameter handling issues, and .NET file-tampering and denial-of-service issues.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes Ubuntu and Microsoft .NET. These notices explicitly affect Ubuntu releases and Ubuntu-packaged .NET runtime/SDK components.
- Source: Ubuntu Security Notices: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices; USN-8426-1: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8426-1; USN-8420-1: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8420-1

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for Chrome desktop fleets because the fresh advisory includes critical browser vulnerabilities. Ubuntu systems should be reviewed through normal security update processes, with extra attention to exposed or privileged uses of the affected components such as kernel Azure images, OpenStack Mistral/Ironic, and Ubuntu-packaged .NET workloads.
